skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-meta-advanced-matching
skill.description: Verify Meta Advanced Matching for Lightspeed eCom C-Series through Product Metrics. Check consent settings, confirm delivery with a paid test order, and diagnose missing purchases or low Event Match Quality.
skill.summary: Check consent and verify Meta Advanced Matching for Lightspeed purchases through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or ordinary account setup. The retained alerts concern CLI and remote tool trust, access to order data, and an unpinned installer. The workflow also permits credential collection and authenticated writes without a general approval step; no evidence of audit-directed prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows the assistant to request integration credentials and pass them to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the Product Metrics app or a dedicated secret input. Remove instructions to collect credentials in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: Product Metrics writes do not require approval before changes are made.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only checks. Show the workspace, property, destination, and expected effect, then get approval before changing settings or sending a test event.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs a local CLI and offers a remote MCP service without a trust check.
remediation.suggestion: Require a verified CLI installation and an explicitly configured Product Metrics MCP server. Limit tool calls to operations needed for matching verification.

remediation.issue: The order lookup can return business data unrelated to the test.
remediation.suggestion: Use the specific test order and request only delivery status. Suppress unrelated order details, margins, and customer classifications from tool results and summaries.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the installer package or the skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Use a verified installer version and an immutable source revision. Keep installation separate from the tracking workflow and require explicit consent before running it.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Advanced Matching for Lightspeed
content.value_statement: Lightspeed purchases can be missing from Meta reports when consent or matching is not configured correctly. Use Product Metrics to check your settings and verify delivery with a paid test order.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status for the selected company and property through the CLI or MCP.
Guide the merchant to verify the connected Meta pixel and select the supported consent banner used on the storefront.
Explain which matching fields Product Metrics hashes and which fields it sends without hashing.
Separate the connection test from verification with a paid test order and the storefront tracking endpoints.
Troubleshoot missing purchases using consent settings, destination status, and the documented event age limit.
limitations: The workflow is for Lightspeed eCom C-Series and requires Product Metrics Pro, Cloudflare, and an existing Meta Conversions API setup.
An authorized person completes steps in the Lightspeed back office, Cloudflare, and Meta Events Manager.
A connection test does not validate customer matching. Matching verification needs a paid test order with ad user data consent.
The workflow does not configure bidding, import past orders, or revise events already sent when a refund occurs.

use_cases.title: Confirm Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether your Lightspeed store, Product Metrics property, and Meta pixel are ready before you place a test order.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Meta Purchases
use_cases.description: Review consent, event delivery, and order timing before investigating a low Event Match Quality score.

use_cases.title: Validate a Tracking Installation
use_cases.description: Verify the Cloudflare tracking endpoints and confirm that a paid test order arrives for the linked property.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What must already be set up for Advanced Matching on my Lightspeed C-Series store? Give me a checklist before I change any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are preparing to configure matching for the first time.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: My storefront uses Cookiebot. Show me where to verify the banner in Product Metrics and explain what happens when a shopper declines ad user data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your Meta destination is connected, but you have not verified your consent settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Paid Order Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Meta accepted the connection test. Explain how I can verify a consented paid test order and what I should expect in Product Metrics and Events Manager.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to distinguish a successful connection from live order delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Missing Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Review setup status for my selected Product Metrics property without changing settings. Explain how to distinguish consent, event age, and destination problems for my test order.
prompt_templates.scenario: A paid test order arrived in Product Metrics but is missing from Meta.

output_examples.input: Meta accepted the connection test. Does that prove matching works?
output: The connection test confirms that Meta accepts events from the destination.
Place and pay for a test order after allowing ad user data. Check that the order appears under the linked property and that Meta receives it.

output_examples.input: My test order appears in Product Metrics but not in Meta. What should I check?
output: Verify that Configure consent names the banner on your storefront and that the test allowed ad user data.
If the order was marked paid more than seven days after checkout, Meta rejects the event.
If consent and timing are correct, check the destination's delivery status in Product Metrics.

best_practices: Verify the selected workspace, property, and Meta pixel before approving any setup change.
Enter API keys and access tokens directly in the Product Metrics app, not in chat.
Use a dedicated paid test order and verify that the banner recorded ad user data consent.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful connection test as proof that a purchase reached Meta with matching data.
Changing or bypassing consent settings just to make a missing event appear.
Listing unrelated customer orders or sharing their details to diagnose a single test order.

faq.question: Is there a separate Advanced Matching switch?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics adds available matching data to eligible events once the Meta destination is saved and the shopper grants ad user data consent.

faq.question: Which customer information does Meta receive?
faq.answer: Product Metrics hashes available identifiers such as email, phone, name, postcode, country, and customer ID. It sends IP address and browser user agent without hashing.

faq.question: What happens if a shopper declines ad user data?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not send that event to Meta. Meta browser and click IDs also require ad storage consent.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta can count browser and server events once when they share the same event name and event ID within 48 hours.

faq.question: Can this import old orders or update refunds?
faq.answer: No. Meta rejects events more than seven days old, and later refunds or cancellations do not change events already sent.

faq.question: Can I use this without the Product Metrics CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the configured Product Metrics MCP server or follow the manual steps in the Product Metrics app.
